BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF EL PASO )
 ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 ELECTRIC RATES                              )

                    ORDER GRANTING APPEARANCES PRO HAC VICE

         THIS MATTER comes before the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

(“Commission”) upon El Paso Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Motion for Admission of William A.

Faulk, III to Appear Pro Hac Vice (“Faulk Motion”) and EPE’s Motion for Admission of Eleanor

D’Ambrosio to Appear Pro Hac Vice (“D’Ambrosio Motion”) (collectively, the “Motions”) filed

on February 10, 2026, and EPE’s Notices of Errata filed on February 12, 2026.

         The Commission grants the Motions, and admits William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor

D’Ambrosio to appear pro hac vice before the Commission in this matter, for the reasons discussed

below.

                                            BACKGROUND

         1.      The Motions filed by EPE request that William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor

D’Ambrosio be admitted to appear before the Commission pro hac vice as co-counsel for EPE in

association with local counsel Jeffrey J. Wechsler of Spencer Fane LLP in Santa Fe, New Mexico. 1

         2.      The Declaration of William A. Faulk, III attached to the Faulk Motion asserts that

William A. Faulk, III is a member in good standing of the State Bar of Texas (“SBOT”), that he is

not under any SBOT administrative or disciplinary investigation, and that he will conduct himself

in accordance with the rules governing attorneys admitted to practice before the Commission and

in the State of New Mexico. 2




1 Faulk Motion (Feb. 10, 2026) at 1; see also D’Ambrosio Motion (Feb. 10, 2026) at 1.
2 Faulk Motion, Ex. A at 1.
         3.       Similarly, the Declaration of Eleanor D’Ambrosio attached to the D’Ambrosio

Motion asserts that Eleanor D’Ambrosio is a member in good standing of the SBOT, that she is

not under any SBOT administrative or disciplinary investigation, and that she will conduct herself

in accordance with the rules governing attorneys admitted to practice before the Commission and

in the State of New Mexico. 3

        4.       Additionally, EPE’s Notices of Errata attached the required Registration

Certificates for Non-Admitted Lawyers, which were filed with the New Mexico State Bar, for

William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor D’Ambrosio. 4

        5.       The thirteen-day time period for responses to the Motions passed, 5 and no party

filed a response to the Motions or Notices of Errata.

                                           DISCUSSION

        6.       In accordance with Rule 1.2.2.9(E) NMAC “[a]n attorney licensed in a jurisdiction

other than New Mexico may appear at public hearings before the [C]ommission or presiding

officer provided such non-resident attorney files a motion pro hac vice and is associated with and

accompanied by an attorney licensed in New Mexico.”

        7.       Pursuant to Rule 24-106 NMRA, an attorney authorized to practice law in another

jurisdiction may perform legal services on behalf of a party, even though the attorney is not

licensed to practice law in New Mexico. 6 For each matter in which the foreign attorney intends to

appear, the attorney must file a registration certificate with the State Bar of New Mexico 7 and

certify that the attorney: is in good standing in another United States jurisdiction; has not been


3 D’Ambrosio Motion, Ex. A at 1.
4 See Notices of Errata (Feb. 12, 2026).
5 See Rule 1.2.2.12(C)(1)(a) NMAC.
6 Rule 24-106(A) NMRA.
7 Rule 24-106(B) NMRA.

 disciplined, suspended, or disbarred in any jurisdiction; has not had a pro hac vice admission

revoked in any jurisdiction; will comply with applicable statutes, laws, and procedural rules in

New Mexico; and will comply with New Mexico’s Rules of Professional Conduct, the Rules

Governing Discipline, the Rules Governing the New Mexico Bar, and relevant procedural rules. 8

        8.       William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor D’Ambrosio each assert that they are members

of a bar in good standing in another jurisdiction, that they are not under any administrative or

disciplinary investigations, and that they will conduct themselves in accordance with New

Mexico’s Rules.

        9.       The Registration Certificates attached to EPE’s Notices of Errata demonstrate that

William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor D’Ambrosio have complied with the requirements set forth in

Rule 24-106 NMRA. 9

                                   FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS

        The Commission finds and concludes:

        10.      The Motions and Notices of Errata were properly filed in accordance with Rules

1.2.2.9(E) NMAC and 24-106 NMRA.

        11.      William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor D’Ambrosio have satisfied the requirements to

practice before the Commission in this matter pro hac vice.

        12.      The Motions should be granted.

        13.      EPE should update the Service Notification list in the docket through PRCe360 to

include William A. Faulk, III and Eleanor D’Ambrosio.

        IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      EPE’s Motion for Admission of William A. Faulk, III to appear in this proceeding

pro hac vice as co-counsel for EPE in association with local counsel Jeffrey J. Wechsler of Spencer

Fane LLP in Santa Fe, New Mexico is GRANTED.

       B.      EPE’s Motion for Admission of Eleanor D’Ambrosio to appear in this proceeding

pro hac vice as co-counsel for EPE in association with local counsel Jeffrey J. Wechsler of Spencer

Fane LLP in Santa Fe, New Mexico is GRANTED.

       C.      EPE shall update the Service Notification in this docket to reflect the admissions

granted in this Order.

       D.      This Order is effective when signed.

       E.      In computing time in accordance with statute, regulation, or Commission order, the

computation shall begin on the date that this Order is filed with the Chief Clerk of the

Commission’s Records Management Bureau or the Chief Clerk’s designee.

       SIGNED under the Seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, this 5th day of

March, 2026.

                         NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

                         /s/ Greg Nibert, electronically signed
                         GREG NIBERT, COMMISSIONER
